one_line: How elaborate scams actually work — the psychology, the mechanics, and the moment the mark realizes — broken down in 45-second hits.
pillars: Modern digital scams (phishing, AI, crypto, marketplace)
Dark patterns & legal deception companies use
audience: Curious skeptics 18-45 who like true-crime, business breakdowns, and 'how it actually works' content. People who think they're too smart to be scammed — and their parents.
tone: Calm, forensic, slightly chilling. Explain the mechanism like a case study, never like a tutorial. Sympathy for victims, never mockery. Always end on the tell that would have saved them.
hook_templates: This scam worked because it was designed to look fake.
{x} works because every single step feels normal.
By the time anyone recognizes {x}, it is already too late.
Here's the exact psychology that makes {x} work on smart people.
Nobody falls for {x}. They fall for the thing that comes before it.
title_keywords: why scammers ask for gift cards

x: a cloned voice on the phone

hard_rules: Educate about the deception, never provide operational instructions for committing it.
Show the manipulation from the victim's side: what they saw, what they felt, what they missed.
Every video ends with the tell, the warning sign, or how it was exposed.
Never mock victims. The thesis is always 'this would work on you too.'
Use only public, widely reported cases. No naming private individuals.
No celebrity likenesses, no bodycam or courtroom footage, no copyrighted assets.
